title: Square and cube roots
status: draft: written by Claude, waiting for owner review

hints.exp.roots.perfect: A square root asks: what times itself makes this? A cube root: what times itself three times?
hints.exp.roots.estimate: Find the perfect squares just below and just above the number. The root is between their roots.
hints.exp.roots.rational: Rational means it can be written as a fraction of whole numbers. Perfect-square roots, fractions, ending and repeating decimals are rational; √2 and π aren't.
hints.exp.roots: Square root: what times itself? Between perfect squares for an estimate. Rational: can it be a fraction?

misconceptionMessages.exp.root-halved: A square root isn't half: √64 = 8, because 8 × 8 = 64.
misconceptionMessages.exp.root-divided: A cube root isn't a third: ∛27 = 3, because 3 × 3 × 3 = 27.
misconceptionMessages.exp.cube-root-sign: A cube root of a negative number is negative: (−2) × (−2) × (−2) = −8.
misconceptionMessages.exp.roots-all-irrational: Not every square root is irrational: √16 = 4, a whole number, so it's rational.
misconceptionMessages.exp.repeating-irrational: A repeating decimal is a fraction (0.333… = 1/3), so it's rational.
misconceptionMessages.exp.pi-rational: π goes on forever without repeating; 3.14 is only close. π is irrational.

sections.title: Square and cube roots
explain: Squaring and square roots undo each other: 7² = 49, so √49 = 7.
A cube root undoes cubing: 3³ = 27, so ∛27 = 3.
sections.key: √ asks: what number times itself makes this? ∛ asks: what number times itself three times?

sections.title: Estimate a square root
sections.objective: Say which two whole numbers √50 is between.
explain: Most numbers aren't perfect squares, so their square roots aren't whole numbers.
Squeeze it between the perfect squares on either side.
sections.key: Find the perfect squares just below and above the number. √50: 49 < 50 < 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8.

sections.title: Rational or irrational?
sections.objective: Tell rational numbers (fractions) from irrational ones (√2, π).
explain: Rational numbers can be written as a fraction of whole numbers. That includes whole numbers, decimals that end, and decimals that repeat.
Irrational numbers go on forever without repeating: √2, √20, π.
sections.key: Can it be written as a fraction? Yes: rational. A square root of a number that isn't a perfect square, or π: irrational.

sections.title: Putting it together
sections.objective: Roots, estimates and rational numbers, mixed.
sections.key: √: what times itself. Estimate between perfect squares. Rational: can it be a fraction?
